tagline: Lumber towns give way to the Wolf River.
intro: From Hiles on Highway 32, the drive runs south through Crandon toward the Wolf River country around Langlade. Crandon lies on the northern shore of Metonga Lake. It began as Ayr, after the town in Scotland, and was incorporated in 1909 under the name of Frank Crandon, the railroad tax commissioner who helped get Forest County created.
Farther south the road enters the town of Langlade, which the Wolf River crosses from northwest to southeast on its way, by the Fox River watershed, to Green Bay.

moments.title: Hiles
moments.text: Named for the lumber baron F. P. Hiles, the community kept a post office from 1903 to 1968.

moments.title: Crandon
moments.text: Lumber companies recruited loggers from Kentucky and moved a sawmill up from Glasgow; the town still holds Kentuck Days for those ancestors.

moments.title: Lily
moments.text: Here the Lily River joins the Wolf, and the old Soo Line grade, its tracks pulled up in 2001, now carries the Wolf River State Trail.
